unit.why: A single anecdote: a hasid twice tells the Rebbe of Peshischa about a dream in which his father says he can lead the world, and the Rebbe answers him wryly.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי איך שהיה חסיד אחד אצל
stories.summary_en: A hasid twice tells the Rebbe of Peshischa that his dead father came to him in a dream and said he could lead the world. The rebbe replies that he should tell his father he is ready, but the main thing is for the father to appear in a dream to the world, so that people travel to him.

tags.why: The father's dream visitation drives the story.

quotes: אני מודיעך שאתה יכול להנהיג העולם
tags.why: The dead father's soul brings a message.

quotes: רק עיקר לראות שיבא בחלום אל העולם שיסעו אצלך
tags.why: The rebbe answers with an ironic witticism.
The hasid's pretension to leadership is gently mocked.

quotes: בא ג״כ החסיד הנ״ל אצל הרה״ק וסיפר לו
tags.why: A hasid comes to the rebbe with his report.
The exchange is between the rebbe and his hasid.
The story turns on who is fit for tsaddik-leadership and on followers travelling to a leader.

quotes: שיבא בחלום אל העולם שיסעו אצלך
tags.why: The rebbe's punchline refers to people travelling to a tsaddik.

missing_concepts: irony or skepticism toward dream claims
